questions.stem: Practice Bulletin 183 defines postpartum hemorrhage as:

options.text: At least 1000 mL, or less if she has signs of hypovolemia, within 24 hours
A hematocrit drop of any size

questions.explanation: The reVITALize definition is at least 1000 mL, or blood loss with hypovolemia, within 24 hours, any route.

options.text: Increase supervision, even though it is not yet the 1000 mL definition
Be called normal after a vaginal birth

questions.explanation: That range increases supervision. After a vaginal birth, more than 500 mL is abnormal.

questions.stem: The first moves for pad after soaked pad are:

options.text: Call for help, massage the uterus, and start a uterotonic

questions.explanation: Treat while blood is sent. The hematocrit lags and does not give permission.

options.text: A cervical tear in every case

questions.explanation: Uterine atony causes about 70 to 80 percent of these bleeds.

questions.explanation: If the uterus is firm and she is still bleeding, tone is not the story.

questions.stem: If massage and uterotonics fail and she is stable enough, the next tool is:

options.text: Tamponade, such as an intrauterine balloon, or surgery if she is crashing

questions.explanation: A crashing patient does not finish a slow ladder.

questions.stem: Around 1500 mL of loss, or abnormal vital signs, you:

options.text: Recheck the hematocrit in the morning
Prepare transfusion while you treat the cause
Wait for tachycardia, which always comes early

questions.explanation: Signs of shock often appear only after the loss is already large.

questions.stem: A hematocrit during the acute bleed:

options.text: Lags, so you do not wait for it to fall
Is the only number that matters

questions.explanation: Hemoglobin and hematocrit are delayed and are not the acute decision.

questions.stem: A firm uterus with continued bright bleeding points to:

options.text: Trauma or another cause that is not atony

questions.explanation: Look for a laceration or retained tissue.

questions.stem: A uterotonic given after every birth is:

options.text: The treatment of an established liter of loss
Prevention, and not the same as treating a bleed in progress

questions.explanation: Prevention with a uterotonic, usually oxytocin, is separate from treating hemorrhage that is already happening.
